Help.title: Help
Help.signInFirst: You need an access token from Settings: <link>sign in</link> first.

start.title: Getting started
start.intro: {app} keeps the articles you want to read later, each with a clean copy and a short summary. Setting it up takes a few minutes.
start.token: Create an access token in Settings for the {safari} Shortcut. The {firefox} add-on gets its own when you click Connect in its options.
start.android: On {android}, <link>install the app</link> and use Share.
start.paste: Anywhere, paste a link at the top of the Inbox.
start.read: Read. A new article shows its summary within about half a minute. Reading and organizing explains the rest.

firefox.title: {firefox} add-on
firefox.intro: A toolbar button, a keyboard shortcut and a right-click menu item that save to {app}.

safari.title: {safari} Shortcut
safari.intro: Save from the Share menu on {iphone}, {ipad} and {mac}. You build it once, and it syncs through iCloud.

android.title: {android}
android.intro: Install {app} from {chrome}, and it appears in every app’s Share menu.

using.title: Reading and organizing
using.intro: What you can do with an article once it is saved.

summaries.heading: Summaries and translations
summaries.text: Every article opens with a one-sentence TL;DR and its key points, in the article’s own language. Under the summary, Translate into shows it in another language, and suggested tags are one tap away. The Aa button sets the theme, colors and font.

preview.heading: “Preview only”
preview.text: Some sites show an article only to readers who are signed in or subscribe. Saved from a link alone, {app} gets just the beginning and marks it “Preview only”; it never gets around a paywall. Open the article signed in to the site and save it again with the extension or the {safari} Shortcut, and the full copy replaces the preview.

organize.heading: Keeping things in order
organize.text: Triage shows unread articles one at a time: read now, later, or archive. Favorites and the Archive keep what you mark, folders and tags group articles, and search looks through titles, summaries and text.

data.heading: Your data
data.text: In Settings, Export downloads everything as JSON or Markdown. You can delete any article at any time.
